warmup.text: This is the last day of the week. In Chapter 23, the plan to hide Naomi goes into action, and the three boys get a visit they will never forget. The poem today is about snowy woods at night. Listen for how quiet it feels.

words.text: Last day with the light roots. Explain why writers use light to talk about understanding. Then build words of your own from Greek and Latin parts, and light the last lanterns of the week.

reading.text: Read Chapter 23 in your book. Watch how the women's plan works, and what the ghosts tell the boys. Then put the week together with your lens: choose the picture that carries the most. Finish with the Virtue Watch.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 23. Then write the final version of your paragraph, with every pronoun clear. Last, explain how a summary and an analysis are different. Copy your work and paste it into Canvas.

do: Tap the highlighted words in the first sentence.
Find the pronoun that could mean two people in the second.
Fix it out loud, then tap Check My Work.
how.why: A pronoun like he, she or they should point to only one person.

do: Read the poem out loud once.
Find the picture you see most clearly.
Read Think About It and keep your answer in mind.
how.why: Poets use pictures instead of telling you what to feel. That is imagery.

do: Tap a word.
Then tap its meaning.
Say out loud how lucid and translucent are different.
how.why: Explaining two close words out loud shows you know them.

do: Read each word and its meaning.
Write one sentence for each word.
Make each sentence show the meaning.
how.why: Using a word in your own sentence is the best proof you know it.

do: Tap the version that names who acted in each pair.
Write one sentence that hides who acted and one that names them.
Explain the difference in the box.
how.why: In writing about history, naming who acted keeps the record true.

do: Decide if each root is Greek or Latin.
Tap a word, then tap its column.
Build two words of your own in the box.
how.why: Knowing where a part comes from helps you build new words.

do: Read today's skill.
Tap your lens for today.
Choose the one picture from this week that carries the most.
how.why: The strongest images in a book are often the ones the author never explains.
how.use: You will use this for question 2.

do: Read Chapter 23 first.
Answer each question in 2 or more sentences.
Use details from the chapter as evidence.
how.why: These questions check what happened and what the author shows you.

do: Write the final paragraph.
Check that every pronoun is clear.
Then explain summary and analysis in the box.
how.why: Today you finish your paragraph and turn it in.

do: Read what perseverance means.
Read the example from this week.
After you read, pick the strongest moment of the week at the end of this tab.
Read the chapter introduction below.
Open your book and read Chapter 23.
Then do the Read Like a Writer box and the Virtue Watch below.

glossary.meaning: a thing in a story that stands for a bigger idea

miss.chronology: Find c-h-r-o-n at the start. Chron means time.
miss.dialogue: Find l-o-g-u-e at the end: dia + logue. Log means word or speech.
miss.evidence: Vid means see, and it comes from Latin.
miss.metaphor: Find p-h-o-r at the end. Phor means carry: a metaphor carries meaning from one thing to another.
miss.narrative: Narr means tell, and it comes from Latin.
miss.perspective: Find s-p-e-c-t in the middle. Spect means look.
miss.protagonist: Prot means first and agon means struggle. Both are Greek.

game.title: Light the Lanterns
game.sub: This week's word game · 4 words today
game.look: Each lantern on the branch waits for one word. Read the meaning, then tap the word parts in order to build the word. When the word is whole, its lantern lights up.

do: Read the meaning under the lantern.
Tap the first part of the word.
Tap the next parts in order.
Tap Next lantern.
how.why: Long words are built from parts. If you know the parts, you can build a word and spell it.

game.doneLine: Every lantern this week is lit. Well done.

words.means: the study of the earth and its places
a clock that keeps very exact time
words.why: chrono (time) + meter (measure). Sailors used them at sea.
lumin (light) + escent. A firefly is luminescent.

art.title: Winter Evening in a Forest
art.alt: A painting of a snowy forest at dusk, with bare trees, a frozen pond and a small sleigh on a snowy road.
art.look: Vilhelm Kyhn painted this winter evening in a forest in Denmark in 1853. It is far from Isaac's road, but it fits the end of Chapter 23: the snow falls thick, and Isaac and Joseph wait in the cold woods by the river.

virtue.name: perseverance
virtue.title: The strongest moment of perseverance this week
virtue.intro: Look back at Chapters 20 to 23. Tap the moment you think shows perseverance the most.

options.t: Naomi keeps saying “No one” to protect Isaac and Nita.
Joseph decides, “Naomi comes with us tonight.”
Naomi runs with the rope still tied to her wrists.
Naomi waits in the dark trunk until the soldiers are gone.
Joseph waits all night in the freezing sleet to keep watch.
